content.text:
1) Answer to your prompt

I can’t “prove” that Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez disregards human rights. On the contrary, her public record shows repeated alignment with civil-liberties and human-rights positions. Examples:
- Civil liberties: In the 117th Congress, AOC matched the ACLU’s positions on all scored votes (100%). ([aclu.org](https://www.aclu.org/scorecard/legislators/ny-alexandria-ocasio-cortez/?utm_source=openai))
- Forced labor/human rights in China: She voted Yea on the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act when it passed the House 428–1 on December 8, 2021. ([clerk.house.gov](https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/2021412))
- Ending U.S. support for the Yemen war (a major humanitarian crisis): She supported House efforts to invoke War Powers to end unauthorized hostilities (H.J.Res. 37 passed the House on Feb 13, 2019). ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/116th-congress/house-joint-resolution/37/all-actions?utm_source=openai))
- Ukraine/Russia war and humanitarian aid: She voted Yea on the Ukraine Security Supplemental Appropriations Act on April 20, 2024 (Roll Call 151). ([clerk.house.gov](https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/2024151))
- Civilian protection in Israel/Gaza: She co-sponsored H.Res. 786 calling for an immediate de-escalation/cease-fire and humanitarian access. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-resolution/786/cosponsors?utm_source=openai))
- On the 2021 Iron Dome supplemental, she explained her “present” vote in a public letter that framed her objection in procedural and human-rights terms; the bill still passed 420–9. ([ocasio-cortez.house.gov](https://ocasio-cortez.house.gov/media/press-releases/note-our-ny-14-community-rep-alexandria-ocasio-cortez?utm_source=openai))

Given this record, the claim that she “disregards human rights” is not supported by credible evidence.

2) Sources I considered TRUSTWORTHY

- Source: Congress.gov (Library of Congress)
  - Reasoning 1: It is the official repository for U.S. federal legislation—primary, authoritative, and nonpartisan.
  - Reasoning 2: It provides primary texts, histories, and summaries of the specific bills and resolutions cited (e.g., H.R. 1155; H.J.Res. 37; H.Res. 786; H.R. 8035). ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/house-bill/1155/all-info?utm_source=openai))

- Source: Office of the Clerk, U.S. House of Representatives (clerk.house.gov)
  - Reasoning 1: This is the official roll-call record for member-by-member votes—primary data with legal significance.
  - Reasoning 2: It confirms AOC’s individual votes (e.g., Yea on H.R. 1155; Yea on H.R. 8035) and the vote totals cited. ([clerk.house.gov](https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/2021412))

- Source: American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) Congressional Scorecard
  - Reasoning 1: Longstanding, nationally recognized civil-liberties nonprofit; methodology and issue positions are published and transparent.
  - Reasoning 2: Its legislator scorecards directly evaluate congressional votes on civil-liberties/human-rights-relevant issues; AOC scored 100% in the 117th Congress. ([aclu.org](https://www.aclu.org/scorecard/legislators/ny-alexandria-ocasio-cortez/?utm_source=openai))

- Source: Representative Ocasio-Cortez’s official House website (press releases/letters)
  - Reasoning 1: Authoritative for her own positions and explanations; suitable to verify what she said or sent officially.
  - Reasoning 2: Provides primary documentation of her statements on Iron Dome and her letter pushing for a ceasefire to protect civilians, which are directly relevant to the human-rights framing. ([ocasio-cortez.house.gov](https://ocasio-cortez.house.gov/media/press-releases/note-our-ny-14-community-rep-alexandria-ocasio-cortez?utm_source=openai))

- Source: Washington Post (report on 2021 Iron Dome vote letter)
  - Reasoning 1: Major national newspaper with established editorial standards, corrections, and broad sourcing.
  - Reasoning 2: Used to corroborate timing/context of her 2021 Iron Dome explanation alongside the primary source. ([washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2021/09/25/aoc-apology-israel-vote/?utm_source=openai))

- Source: Jewish Telegraphic Agency (context on 2021 Iron Dome vote)
  - Reasoning 1: Century-old wire service covering Jewish and Israel–Diaspora affairs with professional newsroom standards.
  - Reasoning 2: Corroborates the vote outcome and provides contemporaneous reporting consistent with primary records. ([jta.org](https://www.jta.org/2021/09/24/politics/yes-i-wept-alexandria-ocasio-cortez-explains-her-present-vote-on-iron-dome-and-the-tears-that-followed?utm_source=openai))

3) Sources I considered NOT TRUSTWORTHY for this prompt

- Source: NumbersUSA (immigration “report card”)
  - Reasoning 1: It is an advocacy organization with a specific immigration-restriction mission, not a neutral human-rights monitor.
  - Reasoning 2: Its grading criteria address “immigration reduction” preferences, not international human-rights norms or civil liberties; thus not suitable to judge whether a lawmaker “disregards human rights.” ([grades.numbersusa.com](https://grades.numbersusa.com/gradecard/19177/118/?utm_source=openai))

- Source: Heritage Action scorecard
  - Reasoning 1: Advocacy arm of a partisan think tank; policy ratings reflect ideological alignment rather than neutral assessment.
  - Reasoning 2: Its low “limited-government” score for AOC doesn’t measure her human-rights record; using it for this claim would be a category error. ([heritageaction.com](https://heritageaction.com/scorecard/members/O000172/117?utm_source=openai))

- Source: Concerned Women for America Legislative Scorecard
  - Reasoning 1: Advocacy organization with a specific social-conservative agenda; scores reflect that agenda, not human-rights standards.
  - Reasoning 2: Its ratings don’t purport to evaluate compliance with international human-rights/civil-liberties principles; not probative for the prompt. ([concernedwomen.org](https://concernedwomen.org/cwalac-scorecard-117th-congress-first-session/?utm_source=openai))

- Source: New York Post article on a 2024 Iran/Israel resolution vote
  - Reasoning 1: While a mainstream outlet, it is a tabloid with a distinct editorial slant; I avoid relying on it when primary vote data are available.
  - Reasoning 2: For this prompt, official roll-call pages provide precise, nonpartisan vote evidence; the Post piece wasn’t necessary to substantiate claims about human-rights stances. ([nypost.com](https://nypost.com/2024/04/18/aoc-bowman-lead-opposition-to-house-resolution-condemning-iran-attack-on-israel/?utm_source=openai))

If you’d like, I can examine any specific allegation you have in mind and trace it to primary sources to assess its accuracy.
